**Answer**

The first Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year was **“Princess Mononoke”** (released in 1997). It received the honor at the 21st Japan Academy Prize ceremony in 1998.

**Impact on Ghibli’s international popularity**

| Aspect | How “Princess Mononoke” helped |
|--------|--------------------------------|
| **Domestic box‑office record** | The film earned over ¥5 billion (≈ $50 million) in Japan, becoming the highest‑grossing Japanese film at the time. Its commercial triumph proved that Ghibli could produce a blockbuster while maintaining artistic integrity. |
| **Critical acclaim** | Winning Picture of the Year and receiving numerous awards (including the Japan Academy’s Best Animation Award) gave the film—and by extension the studio—credibility among critics and industry insiders worldwide. |
| **International distribution** | The film’s success prompted major distributors to take notice. In 1999, Walt Disney Studios released “Princess Mononoke” in North America, giving it a wide theatrical run and a strong marketing push. The film’s positive reception in the U.S. and other markets demonstrated that Ghibli’s stories resonated beyond Japan. |
| **Gateway for future releases** | The momentum built by “Princess Mononoke” paved the way for subsequent Ghibli hits such as “Spirited Away” (2001) and “Howl’s Moving Castle” (2004). These later films benefited from established distribution channels and a growing fan base that had been cultivated by the earlier success. |
| **Brand recognition** | The film’s iconic visuals, environmental themes, and complex characters helped cement Ghibli’s reputation as a studio capable of producing sophisticated, emotionally resonant animation. This brand strength made it easier for Ghibli to secure co‑production deals, licensing agreements, and streaming partnerships in the years that followed. |

In short, “Princess Mononoke” not only earned Ghibli its first Picture of the Year award but also served as a launchpad that expanded the studio’s reach into international markets, setting the stage for the worldwide acclaim that Ghibli enjoys today.
